newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains lower amid sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains lower amid sterling strength.

text.p: LIFFE wheat was again driven lower by a strong sterling, traders said.
Heavy long liquidation by shippers helped drive it down, one said. "It got slammed," he said. But later in the day the sellers dried up and prices recovered.

On the old crop the recovery was helped by profit- taking after new contract lows were reached,, he said. July fell to 91.75 stg, before recovering to 92.50 stg by the close. July volume was 248 lots.
November was the most active month, with 280 of the total 865 lots traded. It last traded 0.85 stg lower at 95.40 stg, having seen a low of 94.75 stg earlier in the day.
Barley also fell, but only nine lots were traded. Five were on January, which last traded 0.75 stg lower at 94.50 stg.

Sterling jumped more than one pfennig and half a cent in Europe after the Bank of England called for a fresh rise in interest rates and warned inflation was likely to overshoot without more policy action.
